clue.text: Strengthen figure, providing secured

indicators.note: the number word holds the conditional word fast inside it, as if keeping it safe

parts.note: forty is a figure, a number
providing, as in 'on condition that', means if

explanation.surface: A military figure ensures something has been made safe and secure.
explanation.definitionFit: To fortify a place or a drink is to make it stronger, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Old girl impressing an attorney, totally

indicators.note: the girl's name presses the other letters into its middle, stamping them inside

parts.note: Nell is a girl's name
taken as written
DA stands for District Attorney, the American prosecutor

explanation.surface: An elderly woman makes a thorough impression on a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means everyone without exception, so it works as a synonym of completely or totally.

clue.text: Work to get tape rolling, for each can roll?

parts.note: toil means hard work

indicators.note: rolling suggests the four letters of the word tape tumbling over into a new order

parts.note: per is Latin-derived for 'for each', as in 'per person'

explanation.surface: Someone labours to unroll sticky tape, asking whether each tin could be rolled too.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN is slang for a lavatory, so a 'can roll' is what hangs beside it; 'rolling' turns TAPE into ETPA.
explanation.definitionFit: The can is slang for the lavatory, and the paper sold on a roll there is its roll.

clue.text: Tail, tongue, but not heart

indicators.note: but not heart says the word for the tongue is used without its central letter

parts.note: a tongue is a language, and Finnish is the language of Finland

explanation.surface: A list of an animal's parts, a tail and a tongue but no heart, as if from a butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: FINNISH has seven letters, so its heart is the fourth, an N; remove it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail of something is its end, its closing part, which is its conclusion.

clue.text: See 19
Combine during the ninth period?

parts.note: during means in, as in 'in the night'
a term is a period, as in a school term
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A question about mixing things together during the ninth period of a school day.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermix things is to blend or mingle them together, a synonym.

clue.text: Haul up poor fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, hauling a word up reads it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: poor quality is bad

explanation.surface: A fisherman lands a disappointing catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab is a small flatfish, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Duck on the water circling lake, little bird

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, so the letter O

indicators.note: circling says the word for damp goes around the letter for lake

parts.note: something on the water is wet
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A duck swimming around a lake is accompanied by a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is called this, so it is a little bird by its very name.

clue.text: Boxers given power over ref, size and girth abused

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the letter for power above the rest

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: abused suggests ill treatment, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Heavyweight boxers, big and broad, rough up the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges REF, SIZE and GIRTH (the 'and' only joins them) to make RIZEFIGHTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prizefighters fight for money, so they are professional boxers.

clue.text: Need bristles? Bug off! You've got them!

definitions.text: Need bristles? Bug off! You've got them!

indicators.note: off, as in gone bad, marks the fifteen letters before it as spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude retort to someone fretting about wanting stubble: go away, your face already has it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the anagram of NEED BRISTLES BUG and also describes someone with fashionable stubble already.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable short beard growth, kept deliberately, is the bristles someone already has.

clue.text: Head scalped in days of yore

indicators.note: scalped says the top, the first letter, is cut off the slang word for a head

parts.note: bonce is British slang for a head

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of scalping from the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time long ago, like the old phrase about yore.

clue.text: Girl claims queen isn't in control over autonomous state

indicators.note: the girl's name claims, or takes hold of, the other letters inside it

parts.note: Suzy is a girl's name
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the queen
ain't is the informal form of isn't

explanation.surface: A girl insists that the queen is not really in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Suzerainty is the power a dominant state holds over a dependent one that runs its own internal affairs.

clue.text: Form seen in flower

parts.note: a carnation is a flower

explanation.surface: A shape spotted among the petals of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An incarnation is a bodily form or embodiment that something takes.

clue.text: Filming of attacks showing dwarf's passing

parts.note: One of Snow White's seven dwarfs, plus the S of the possessive
lapping is passing a slower runner who is a whole lap behind

explanation.surface: Footage of assaults that reveals the death of one of the little men.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a craze of filming assaults on phones; 'passing' looks like death but means overtaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the craze of recording assaults on people with a phone camera for sharing.

clue.text: Bobby plugging pixie's corrected text

indicators.note: plugging says the policeman word is stuffed into the middle of the sprite word

parts.note: a pixie is a fairy
a bobby is British slang for a policeman, a cop

explanation.surface: A policeman promotes a pixie's revised manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean final version of a document, after corrections, is called this.

clue.text: Source of authority we probe, as corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt, as in debased, tells us the letters before it are spoiled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Investigators look into where official power comes from, finding it rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A power base is the support group from which a politician draws strength and influence.

clue.text: Indication appears good, opening evil letters

indicators.note: good is opening the word for evil, prising its letters apart

parts.note: evil is sin
letters come in the post

explanation.surface: A sign that good things appear when one opens nasty letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost is an indicator showing the way, and figuratively any sign of what lies ahead.

clue.text: See 14
Leading British families in the soup?

parts.note: the Browns, of the former Prime Minister Gordon Brown, and the Windsors, the royal family
the Browns, of the former Prime Minister Gordon Brown, and the Windsors, the royal family

explanation.surface: Asks whether the country's top families have got themselves into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' suggests trouble; Brown Windsor is an old British brown meat soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown Windsor is a thick meaty soup once common in British hotels and railway dining cars.

clue.text: Old writer's companion an unpleasant type? No way!

indicators.note: no says the abbreviation for way is to be lost from the longer word

parts.note: a stinkpot is a nasty, contemptible person
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an old writer's friend was a nasty piece of work, and is told no way.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers with dip pens kept a pot of ink at hand, their constant partner at the desk.

clue.text: Native American short of fine fabric

indicators.note: short of says the longer word lacks the letters for fine at its end

parts.note: the Chinook are a Native American people of the Pacific Northwest
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A Native American lacks good-quality cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a hard-wearing cotton twill cloth used for trousers.

clue.text: River with breeze to the east

parts.note: a breeze is a movement of air

explanation.surface: A river with a wind blowing from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, flowing through Leeds.

clue.text: I left book to be returned in describing personal story of all written works

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed short group sits inside the longer adjective

parts.note: biographical writing describes a person's life story

indicators.note: returned, as in sent back, means the three short pieces are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone left a library book to be returned, while describing a life story of all writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be returned' looks like a library instruction for the book, but it reverses the three short pieces, which then sit after the second letter of the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A bibliography lists written works, so the adjective relates to such catalogues of writing.

clue.text: Rest with member of pack?

definitions.meaning: one untruth in a pack of untruths

explanation.definitionFit: Lying down is resting, and a single falsehood belongs to a whole pack of falsehoods.

clue.text: Work sent back, given article on fast food from Italy

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the article after the fast
sent back means the abbreviation for a work is read in reverse

parts.note: OP is the abbreviation for opus, a work
Lent is the Christian period of fasting
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A work is returned along with an article about Italian fast food.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is an Italian dish of boiled cornmeal.
